surfaces.part: canopy shaded underside and front mass

answer.evidence: The main body is the rounded canopy. Its width profile widens from 2 px at row 1 to 43 px at rows 21-25, then narrows through rows 37-47 to the 10 px trunk. That is a lobed dome silhouette. The lit light-green leaf clusters (L~114-132) fill rows 4-25 and read as the upper surface seen from above. Darker clusters (L~41-73) fill rows 26-44, with the darkest shadow at rows 41-44 under the canopy. That is the front and underside. There is no sharp front-edge line, but the light-to-dark change shows a top and a front. The trunk (rows 45-62, width 10-15, brown with roots flaring at rows 55-61) is a vertical shaft with its top hidden by the canopy. Grass tufts at the base are decor. The tree has a top surface and a front face of more than 3 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate canopy is built from broad, blocky clumps in about 4 muted greens, and the trunk is a thin brown column with 2-3 tones. The measured 11 visible tones per tile is well under half the references' 26 and 29, and raw colours total only 27 against 427 and 567. The references have many small leaf clusters, bright highlights, and a branching, rooted trunk, and the candidate's larger smooth planes look softer and simpler beside them. Near-flat coverage is 0% and the edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker outline and no flat fill. The shortfall is in shading depth and texture density: the canopy has few per-leaf highlights and no clumps in several greens, and the trunk and base have little grain. Overall it is clearly thinner than the references.
